To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spontaneous growth hormone release is pulsatile in healthy term infants and that the pulsatile release pattern is different in infants of different ages during the first 4 days of life.

1) GH secretion was pulsatile and that the frequency and amplitude of the pulses were higher in the earlier studied infants; 2) GH secretion was greater in the infants studied earlier after delivery; and 3) there were no significant differences in the characteristics of the GH secretory pattern between male and female term newborns.
spontaneous GH release is present in term infants and that there is a decrease in the frequency, amplitude, and width of GH pulses with increasing postnatal age.

the spontaneous pulsatile GH release in the term infant is greater in the first day of life than in later infancy.
the GH secretion in the newborn is pulsatile and is higher during the first day of life than during the first week of life.

there is spontaneous GH release in the human term newborn.
